messages.content: i wrote the children reads near the window. can you help me make it correct without changing where they are?
write: the children read near the window. children is more than one, and you use read with that group in this sentence.
keep the explanation simple.
the children read near the window. with one child, you could say the child reads near the window.
now make it happening right now with more than one child.
the children are reading near the window.
why are and not is?
because you are talking about children, more than one. the children are reading goes with that group. for one child, you would say the child is reading.
now write a short story with one child reading first and another child coming later.
a child is reading near the window. another child comes into the room and sits with a book. now both children are reading in the same quiet place.
can you keep it in the past instead?
a child was reading near the window. another child came into the room and sat with a book. then both children were reading in the same quiet place.
what changed with are when you moved into the past?
are reading changed to were reading for the children. is reading changed to was reading for one child.
now give only the sentence about both children in the past.
both children were reading in the same quiet place.
i had a friend over for lunch. we turned the radio off to talk, and after they left i forgot to turn it back on. later i found that i had enjoyed the quiet too.
you had two good parts of the day: talking with your friend and then having some quiet after the visit. the radio did not need to be on for either part.
make my idea simple.
we turned the radio off while my friend visited. after they left, i kept it off and liked the quiet.
i want to remember the conversation too. we talked about a book both of us had read.
then you can keep that specific detail: we talked about a book we had both read, then i had a quiet part of the afternoon after the visit.
is had both read saying we read it together at the same time?
not by itself. it says each of you had read the book before the conversation. you could have read it on different days.
we did. i read it last month, and my friend finished yesterday.
then the conversation came after both of you finished, but you read on different days. you can talk about the same story without having read it together.
say it simply.
you read the book last month, and your friend finished yesterday. after that, you talked about it together.
write the whole note with the quiet after they left too.
my friend came for lunch, and we turned the radio off to talk about a book we had both read. after they left, i kept the radio off and enjoyed the quiet too.
write a story about two people who use one desk at different hours for work. the first person leaves it ready for the next, but they do not need to be close friends for the story to work.

one worker used a desk in the morning, and another used it in the afternoon. the morning worker liked having books around, while the afternoon worker needed space for paper. at first, the desk was often too full when the afternoon began. then they talked about what each needed. the morning worker chose a shelf for the books and left one small note about anything still on the desk. the afternoon worker kept the same space clear before leaving. they did not talk much during the day, but their short conversation made the desk work better for both.
make the story simple.

two people used the same desk at different hours for work. one needed books and the other needed space for paper. they talked, then chose a shelf for the books and kept the desk clear for the next person.
does that say they must like all the same things?
no. they found a way to use one place while having different needs. the story does not make them the same person or give them the same work.
write the short conversation that helped them choose.
i need space for paper when i come in. i need my books near while i work. could the books go on this shelf? yes, that keeps them near without taking the whole desk.
can i add that the afternoon worker also helps keep it clear?
yes. that makes the choice something both people do. you can write: before leaving, the afternoon worker put the paper away so the desk was ready for the morning too.
now end with the empty desk, not an explanation.
at the end of the day, the desk was clear, the books were on the shelf, and one chair stood ready for the morning.
i looked at a drawing and saw a red flower near a blue cup. then my sister said there was a small tree at the back too. i had not seen it. does that mean the tree was added after i looked?
not from that alone. it may have been in the drawing while you looked, even though you did not see it. seeing only part of a picture is different from knowing the rest is not there.
say it simply.
the tree could already be in the drawing. you said you did not see it, not that you watched someone add it later.
now i look again and see it. what can i say without saying i saw it the first time?
i see the small tree now. i did not see it when i first looked at the drawing.
ask my last question simply.
what can i say without saying i saw the tree the first time?
my sister says she also did not see the red flower at first. can we both be right about what we saw?
yes. you may each have looked at different parts first. your first answer about the flower and hers about the tree can both come from the same picture.
write a short sentence about that.
we looked at the same drawing, but i saw the red flower first and my sister saw the small tree.
can seeing a blue cup tell me the flower is blue too?
no. the cup is blue in the details you gave, and the flower is red. one object color does not change the other.
if i say i could have helped my cousin, does that mean i did help?
no. could have helped says help was possible before now. it does not by itself say the help happened.
explain simply.
it says you had a possible way to help, but not that you really helped.
now add if they had asked. keep that different from saying they asked.
i could have helped my cousin if they had asked.
does that sentence say my cousin did something wrong because they did not ask?
not by itself. it says what might have happened if they had asked, but does not tell the whole reason for what happened.
answer simply.
it says what might have happened if they had asked. it does not tell us everything about why they did not ask or why you did not help.
make my question simple.
does that sentence say my cousin did something wrong by not asking?
now answer with one short sentence.
no, it gives a possible choice from before, not a whole answer about who did something wrong.
can you make a kind reply instead of talking about who was wrong?
i did not know you needed help. next time, please ask, and i can tell you whether i have time.
my child keeps asking for another story before bed. i like reading with her, but i also need to finish the evening. i want to make the plan clear and kind.
you could make the end clear before reading starts. for example: we will read one story, then put the book away and get ready for sleep.
say the idea simply.
you want to read with your child before bed and still have a clear time to stop. you can say the plan before opening the book.
i do that, but after the story finishes she still wants more.
you can understand that she wants more without changing the plan every time. you could say: i liked reading with you too. that was our story for this evening, and we can choose another for tomorrow.
write my last detail simply.
after the story finishes, she still wants another one.
i want to give her something to choose, but not whether we stop reading now.
you could ask which book she would like to keep ready for tomorrow. that gives her a real choice while keeping your plan to stop reading for this evening.
make the question.
which book would you like to have ready for tomorrow evening?
what if she says she wants the same story again tomorrow?
that can be a clear choice too. if she wants the same story, her choice is still real. you can put that book where both of you will find it tomorrow.
i left a book at the house of my aunt, but the message i am writing is to my sister. i need to ask if she can get it when she visits our aunt. make the people clear.
could you bring my book back when you visit our aunt? i left it at her house.
write my request using the house of my aunt.
i left a book at the house of my aunt, and i want to ask my sister to get it when she visits.
now ask my sister without saying she has already said yes.
could you bring my book back when you visit our aunt?
use could in a simple question.
could you bring my book back when you visit our aunt?
what if she says she is not visiting this week?
then you need another plan for getting the book. her answer does not change whose book it is or tell you it is not there. it only says that visit is not happening this week.
answer simply.
then that way of getting the book will not work this week. you can ask about another time or choose another way to get it.
now i will ask my aunt to keep it until i come. write that message.
could you keep my book there until i visit? i will get it from you then.
say my last plan simply.
i will ask my aunt to keep the book until i come to get it.
picoboi, ask me one question about reading, then wait for my answer.
what do you like to read when you have a quiet hour?
i like short stories. now ask one question about that answer, not something different.
what do you like about short stories?
say my request simply.
ask one question about my answer, not something different.
i like to finish one before i need to leave. i do not want to stop while i am still reading it.
then a short story can work well with the time you often have. you can reach the end before moving to the next part of your day.
say that idea simply.
you like a story you can finish before you need to leave or do something else.
now do not ask another question. just write one sentence about what i said.
you like short stories because you can finish one in the time you have.
can you know from that which story i like best?
no. you gave a reason you like short stories, but not the name of a specific one.
ask my last question simply.
do you know which story i like best from what i said?
